page: Amazon Web Services c9g.8xlarge is a compute-optimized server powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs based on the 64-bit ARMv9 architecture (Neoverse-V3 model) running at 3.3 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 17 Gbps. No GPUs are included.

Benchmark results indicate strong compute and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core (2382.0) and multi-core (25987.0) metrics, alongside high performance in software compilation with Clang (63901.0) and static web serving throughput (92.57 GB/sec). Passmark database operations (47005.39) and memory scores (4502.98) also rank in the top tier. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng (63991.52) and Redis SET operations (93.19 million operations/sec) fall into the strong category. However, uncached large-block memory read and write speeds, as well as single-core stress-ng performance, remain in the average tier.

Given its ARM64 architecture and dedicated core allocation, the c9g.8xlarge offers high compute density and power efficiency relative to its hardware profile. The absence of hyperthreading (1.0 thread per core) ensures predictable execution times, making it highly suitable for compute-bound workloads. The server is optimized for tasks such as software compilation, high-throughput static web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded decompression. It is also capable of handling moderate LLM inference tasks for small to medium models, though it lacks hardware acceleration for larger AI workloads.
